subject: Materials Science
title: Copper: Humanity's First Metal
description: A quick win: understand Copper: Humanity's First Metal.

hook.text: Around 9,000 years ago, someone picked up a green rock and hammered it flat.

buildup.text: That rock was native copper — soft enough to shape without smelting or furnaces.

discovery.text: Copper conducts electricity second only to silver and resists corrosion for centuries.

twist.text: The Statue of Liberty's copper skin has turned green but hasn't corroded through in 140 years.

climax.text: Every electric motor, power line, and circuit board depends on copper's conductivity.

punchline.text: Civilization's first metal still powers civilization.

quiz.question: What makes copper essential to modern technology?
options: It is the hardest non-ferrous metal
It is the lightest metal available
